title: Risk-shaped release scripting and experiment log (working)
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working doc for a "risk-shaped" approach to feature releases and experiments. The goal: combine scripted operational steps (so runbooks are executable) with explicit experiment logging and risk budgeting so product, SRE, and solutions can run coordinated canaries or ABs without ad-hoc adoptions.

Why 'risk-shaped'?
- Not every feature needs identical exposure. We should size exposure and observability to the risk vector (privacy, cost-per-token, latency amplification, hallucination risk, surface area).
- Make safe defaults: for high behavioral risk features, require stronger telemetry, lower initial slices, and automated rollback hooks.

Audience and usage:
- Primary: product managers and release stewards doing LLMinterface releases (console or API changes)
- Secondary: SRE oncall, solutions engineers handling high-value customers, legal/security for regulatory gated features

Quick glossary (short):
- Steward: person owning the release ceremony and stakeholder calls
- Slice: user cohort / traffic bucket for progressive exposure
- Probe: synthetic traffic sequence used to exercise a known failure mode
- Commitment signal: metric threshold that will trigger investigator or rollback

High-level flow (one-paragraph):
1) Pre-flight: risk assessment and telemetry template populated in PR.
2) Smoke script: automated synthetic probes run against canary route.
3) Micro-exposure: open a small slice (0.1-1% depending on risk) with tight SLO/telemetry.
4) Observation window: live metrics + human sweep (steward + SRE) for 30–120 minutes.
5) Expansion gating: if no commitment signals, step up exposure; otherwise quarantine and revert.

Risk bucket examples and suggested defaults (opinionated):
- Safety-behavioral (hallucination/privacy): start 0.1-0.5% slice, mandatory human sweep, require offline eval on 500 random prompts, rollback threshold: +0.5% downstream complaint rate or NLU regression > 2.5% relative
- Latency/cost: start 1-5% slice, enable tracing and p50/p95 token-level cost, rollback on 30% increase in p95 latency or 2x token-unit cost
- Capacity/throughput: start 2-10% with CPU/GPU autoscale policy attached, synthetic load probes required, rollback if error rate > 0.5% or provisioned capacity exhausted

Operational scripts (playbook snippets you can copy into ops chat):
- preflight-check.sh (example steps)
  - validate-schema: check model config vs catalog (model-version pinned?)
  - telemetry-hook: ensure new metrics are registered in console (metric IDs listed in PR)
  - synthetic-probe: run 20 probes across top 3 locales (fail if > 2 errors)

- open-slice (example sequence for steward)
  1) run preflight-check.sh and paste results into experiment log
  2) enable route flag for cohort X at 0.5%
  3) post message to #release-ops: "slice open: feature-xyz, 0.5%, steward=Avery"
  4) start observation timer and screen-share for first 10 minutes

Measurement plan (what we watch and where):
- Availability: 5xx and 4xx errors per-minute (source: console/observability)
- Latency: p50/p95 token generation time (console route view)
- Quality signals: sentiment drift, hallucination detector score, rerank rejection rate (where applicable)
- Business KPIs: CTR on new UI, conversion lift, refunds or escalation tickets (Zendesk)
- Cost: token units per request and cost-per-1000-requests

Commitment signals (examples to wire to automations):
- Trigger investigator: any of these
  - sustained >2x baseline p95 latency for 10 minutes
  - incremental error rate > 0.4% on new route for 5 minutes
  - sketchy safety score > threshold for 3 unique users in 15 minutes
- Auto-rollback:
  - same conditions extended to 30 minutes OR explicit ReversionPolicy tag in PR

Experiment logging template (fill on every release/experiment):
- experiment_id: string (use ISO date + short slug)
- steward: name
- start_time: ISO timestamp
- initial_slice: e.g., "0.5% web-US-cohortA"
- risk_bucket: one of [safety, latency, capacity, compliance]
- telemetry_refs: list of metric IDs
- probes_executed: short list (probe IDs)
- pass_criteria: short bullets (e.g., no p95 regressions, no complaint spikes)
- abort_criteria: short bullets
- postmortem_owner: name

Run log (short template to paste into Slack thread during rollout):
- T+0: preflight complete, probes OK (attach logs)
- T+5: slice opened 0.5% (notes: traffic source distribution)
- T+15: first sweep complete, no signal anomalies
- T+45: p95 up 10% but under threshold; continue
- T+120: decision: expand to 2% (or rollback) with reason and proximate metric

Examples (past quick cases):
- Case 2024-11-small-rerank: we opened at 1%, latency up 12% p95, rerank accuracy neutral. Decision: scope micro-optimizations, stayed at 1% for 36 hours. Lesson: enable token-level cost alarms and cheaper quantized fallback.
- Case 2024-12-privacy-filter: started 0.1% only; probe triggered user data leakage pattern on synthetic sequence; immediate rollback and audit. Lesson: add pre-deploy synthetic sequences for PII patterns.

Open questions (needs decisions):
- Who signs off on an exception to the 'human sweep required' rule for safety-behavioral features? (suggest: Head of Product or delegated steward)
- Are we comfortable wiring auto-rollback for customer-tiered traffic (enterprise customers) or should enterprise customers be excluded by default?
- Do we want a 'fast-track' protocol for urgent security fixes that bypass the small-slice progression? If so, what limits?

Short checklist for PR authors (copy into PR description):
- [ ] risk bucket selected and justified
- [ ] experiment logging template added to PR
- [ ] telemetry metric IDs included and instrumented
- [ ] probe script added and green locally
- [ ] steward named and calendar block for observation window

Tactical next steps (2-week sprint):
- Build a lightweight experiment-logging form in Console that auto-populates metric hooks (owner: Sasha)
- Create a small runbook automation to open/close slices via API (owner: Diego)
- Draft exception policy for enterprise traffic (owner: Avery)

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep templates short — long ceremony reduces adoption.
- Prefer executable checklists and paste-ready Slack snippets so stewards can follow without extra typing.
- This doc is intentionally procedural; long-form risk taxonomy should live in Confluence and link here.

Appendix: quick links and probes (copy into PR):
- Probe script: github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/probes/basic-safety-check.sh
- Slack channel for ops posts: #release-ops
- Example experiment id format: 2025-01-15-riskshape-xyz

End working notes. Will iterate with SRE and Solutions this week.
